title: The shipped catalog points an agent at documents the package does not contain
foundBy: user report (host), asking during review: "if someone just installs the npm package, but not the repo, how do they see/read the docs?"

evidence.verified:
`npm run stage` was run and the staged directory read, rather than the source. All 49 catalog entries in `.package/catalog.json` carry an absolute `spec`, and 0 remain relative. The first reads `https://github.com/codesweep-ai/ui/blob/<sha>/components/AgentStatus.md`, where the sha matches `dist/BUILD.json` exactly. `.package/package.json` carries a `homepage` pinned to the same commit, and no `scripts` or `devDependencies`. The repository's own `catalog.json` is unmodified.

`npm run test:stage-package` passes 10 tests. Neutering the rewrite and its guard, while leaving both exports in place, fails the two catalog tests and leaves the README tests passing. So the new tests measure the new behaviour rather than the existence of a function. `npm run ci` exits 0 at adf111e, with the visual gate comparing 112 of 112 captures at 0 differing pixels.

details:
`catalog.json` ships in the package and the markdown documents do not. The `files` list is `dist`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `catalog.json` and `README.md`.

Every catalog entry carries a `spec` field holding a relative path, such as `components/AgentStatus.md`. That path resolves against a repository the reader does not have, so it points at nothing inside the installed package.

This hits the audience the catalog is for. `scripts/stage-package.mjs` ships it on the grounds that it is the index this project tells an agent to read first, and `AGENTS.md` says to search the catalog before building any UI. So an agent installs the package, opens the index it was directed to, follows a component's pointer and finds no file, no address and no commit.

`package.json` has the same weakness in a smaller way. Its `homepage` is the repository's readme at the default branch, carrying no version. The manifest is the usual first stop inside an installed package. An agent inspecting it is sent to documentation for whatever the default branch holds, rather than for the version in front of it.

The README is already handled correctly, which is what makes the other two look like oversights rather than a decision. `scripts/stage-package.mjs` rewrites its relative links into absolute repository URLs pinned to the commit recorded in `dist/BUILD.json`, and refuses to stage when that file is missing or records no sha. All seven documents the readme links to exist at 1638d27, the commit `v0.3.0` was built from.

Pinning to a commit is the right mechanism rather than a workaround. The documentation site is built and deployed only from the default branch, with no per-version path. So a link to the site would show a reader on an older version the documentation for a newer one.

The fix is to give `catalog.json` the rewrite the readme already gets, so each `spec` becomes an absolute URL pinned to the same sha. `homepage` needs pinning the same way. Both keep one source of truth in the repository and make the shipped copy able to locate itself.

notes.text: Nobody working in this repository can meet this, because `components/` is on disk and every relative path resolves. It only appears from an installed package, which is the shape this ledger keeps finding. A failure that cannot occur where the work is done reports itself to whoever is downstream.

The fix reuses the shape the README already had rather than inventing one. `publishedCatalog` and `publishedManifest` sit beside `publishedReadme`, take the same commit, and carry the same guard: nothing reaches the tarball still pointing at a path the reader has not got. The catalog's guard also rejects an entry carrying no `spec` at all, because an entry that points nowhere is the same dead end by another route.

The staged catalog's generated note now names the commit its specs point at, so a reader holding only the package can tell which version they are reading about.
